about: Figures behind the data essay traditional-crafts-basic-income (why Japan's traditional crafts are losing their makers, pay against the minimum wage, and what a basic income or Ireland's Basic Income for the Arts would add). Each fact gives its value, the date or period it refers to, the source and the day it was checked. build.js checks that every language of the essay carries the digits listed under 'digits' (any one of the alternatives in a nested list), and recomputes the monthly minimum wage, the hourly rate of the ¥120,000 offer, the totals with a basic income, the cost per worker and the Irish yearly amount and odds from this file and data/japan-2026.json.

hook.note: an X post viewed about two million times by a craft-school graduate: the job offers reaching the school were almost all about ¥120,000 a month (額面), not enough to live on; a private individual, so not linked. Not a survey; the essay does not check it

facts.unit: traditional crafts designated by the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry
facts.note: 「国が指定した伝統的工芸品244品目（2025年10月27日時点）」; the latest designation, 東京手彫り印章 (Tokyo hand-carved seals), announced by the Kanto Bureau of Economy, Trade and Industry on 27 October 2025

facts.unit: workers
facts.note: 「従業者数も1979年の28.8万人がピーク」, from the Association for the Promotion of Traditional Craft Industries' data as cited in a paper by the Japan Craft Sangyo Association for the SME Agency's small business policy subcommittee (12 October 2018); no METI or Association document stating it directly was found

facts.unit: JPY production
facts.note: 「1974年の3,840億円から1983年の5,410億円まで増加」, same document as peakWorkers (Association data as cited); a 2010 JAIST conference paper gives ¥523.7 billion for 1983

facts.unit: JPY production of the designated crafts
facts.note: 「平成10年度に約2,784億円であったところ、29年度には約927億円となっており、約67％減少」 (MIC Administrative Evaluation Bureau, June 2022, p. 25 of the report)

facts.unit: JPY production of the designated crafts
facts.note: down about 67% from FY1998 (same report)

facts.unit: workers in the designated crafts
facts.note: 「平成10年度の約11万5,000人から29年度の約5万8,000人まで半減」 (same report, p. 39)

facts.unit: workers in the designated crafts
facts.note: same report

facts.unit: workers in the designated crafts
facts.note: 「従業員数は緩やかな減少傾向にあり、令和４年度は約4.8万人」; 「生産額は、平成28年度に1,000億円を下回って以降、漸減傾向」 (no FY2022 production figure in the text); METI explanatory material for the Agency for Cultural Affairs' council, July 2026, p. 5, from the Association's data

facts.unit: % of workers aged 50 and over, 70 and over, and up to their 20s
facts.note: 「50歳代以上が63.6％と半数超。特に70歳代以上は18.0％と、20歳代までの6.0％よりも多い」 (same METI material, p. 5); 30s-40s 30.3%, 50s-60s 45.6%

facts.unit: years within which the number of workers could halve (METI)
facts.note: METI secretariat paper for the 15th meeting of its entertainment and creative policy study group: workers could halve within ten years; some workshops turn down would-be apprentices 「稼げないから」 (because the work does not pay)

facts.unit: JPY, METI traditional crafts support budget
facts.note: 「伝統的工芸品産業「支援」補助金 3.6億円」 (successor training, raw materials, new products; 「令和8年度：84件採択（令和7年度採択数：82件）」, subsidy rate 2/3 for associations and makers) and 「「振興」補助金 7.2億円」 (to the Association), 「合計 10.8億円」 (same METI material, pp. 8-10)

facts.unit: JPY an hour, national weighted average minimum wage
facts.note: 「改定額の全国加重平均額は1,177円（昨年度1,121円）」; in force between 1 October and 2 December 2026 by prefecture; highest ¥1,280 (Tokyo), lowest ¥1,085 (Miyazaki) (MHLW, 3 September 2026)

facts.unit: working hours a month used by MHLW to compare the minimum wage with public assistance
facts.note: 「月173.8時間働いた場合」, material 「生活保護と最低賃金」 for the Central Minimum Wages Council's subcommittee on guidelines (second meeting, 10 July 2026), as posted by the Niigata Labour Bureau

facts.unit: JPY scheduled monthly earnings (所定内給与額), all general workers
facts.note: 2025 Basic Survey on Wage Structure, summary (MHLW, March 2026): 「男女計 340,600円（前年比3.1％増）」; June pay, firms with 10 or more employees

facts.unit: JPY scheduled monthly earnings of general workers: ceramic and stone products, wood and paper products, textile and clothing production workers
facts.note: e-Stat, 2025 Basic Survey on Wage Structure, general workers by occupation, table 1 (industries total, firms with 10 or more employees): ¥283.9 thousand, ¥269.7 thousand, ¥221.0 thousand; there is no category for traditional craft workers

facts.unit: EUR a week to 2,000 artists and arts workers
facts.note: 2,000 recipients picked at random from 8,206 eligible applicants (over 9,000 applications), paid from the selection date of 29 August 2022 for three years, extended for six months to February 2026; taxable; 1,000 eligible applicants in a control group paid €650 a year (Department press releases of 28 October 2022 and 19 June 2025)

facts.unit: hours a week more on creative practice than the control group
facts.note: Impact Assessment (2 years), data October 2022 to October 2024: 11 weekly hours more on creative practice; 14 percentage points more likely to have completed new works; 3.5 weekly hours less working in another sector; 15 points less likely to have felt downhearted or depressed and 16 points less likely to have experienced anxiety; life satisfaction 7 against 6

facts.unit: EUR of benefit to society per EUR of public money
facts.note: Alma Economics cost-benefit analysis for the Department: total gross pilot costs about €114 million between 2021 and 2025 (2025 prices); just over €100 million of benefits, mostly wellbeing

facts.unit: EUR from Budget 2026 for the successor scheme
facts.note: '2,000 eligible artists will be selected to receive the payment of €325 per week. The payment will be for 3 years'; 3-year cycles; selection by anonymised random sampling (Department, 10 February 2026; guidelines of 1 April 2026)

facts.unit: applications to the successor scheme
facts.note: EY selection report of 31 July 2026 (published 4 November 2026); applications open 15 April to 12 May 2026; payments backdated to September 2026; €34.4 million in Budget 2027 (Department, 13 October 2026)

facts.unit: applicants notified on 15 October and on 12 November 2026
facts.note: 'The Department commenced communication to 780 applicants ... on Thursday 15 October and a further 450 applicants will be notified today'; a further tranche before Christmas
